mutants.reason: Inverted reset condition on the read-path block: outputs are not cleared during reset and the read state is cleared during normal operation, so no read can complete.
bvalid is not raised at Ec (set to 0), so no write response is ever given.
Status hit is inverted: 0x40 is treated as unmapped (SLVERR, rdata 0) and every other non-register word index is treated as status.
r_w_held resets to 1, so after reset wready stays 0 and the write-data held state is wrongly set until a B transfer.
The upper bits of the extended word index are 1, so every address compares as out of range: all accesses become unmapped, including registers and status.
Read select is inverted, so a register read returns the OR of the other registers instead of the addressed register.
Byte lane 3 is written when wstrb[3]=0 and kept when wstrb[3]=1, so the lane strobe is inverted.
r_aw_held resets to 1, so awready stays 0 after reset and a held write address is wrongly present after reset.
The write enable selects every register except the addressed one, so the wrong registers are written.
Inverted reset condition on the write handshake block: the handshake outputs are not cleared in reset, and the state is held at reset values in normal operation, so no write handshake works.

The reset value of r_aw_okay is only read through wr_okay when aw_hs=0, and that only matters when wr_commit=1, which needs r_aw_held=1. r_aw_held is only set after an AW transfer, which loads r_aw_okay in the same edge, and reset clears r_aw_held. The reset value therefore never reaches a port.
bvalid and bresp are updated on every edge except Ec, so bvalid is wrongly raised without a completed write and is not raised at Ec.
wready resets to 1, so wready is 1 during reset and in the cycle ending at R1, and a W transfer could occur at R1.
The held write address and decode are captured when there is no AW transfer, not when there is one, so a write whose data or commit comes later uses the wrong register or response.

The reset value of r_aw_reg_hit is only used via wr_reg_hit when aw_hs=0, and then only with wr_commit=1, which needs r_aw_held=1. That state is only reached after an AW transfer has loaded r_aw_reg_hit, and reset clears r_aw_held. The reset value never reaches a port.
Byte lane 0 is written when wstrb[0]=0 and kept when wstrb[0]=1, so the lane strobe is inverted.
rvalid resets to 1, so rvalid is 1 during reset and after R1 with no read in progress.

Inverted reset condition on the held write address/data block: the held decode, data and strobes stay at zero in normal operation, so writes whose AW and W do not arrive at the same edge use wrong data or address.
bvalid resets to 1, so bvalid is 1 during reset and after R1 with no write in progress.
Byte lane 1 is written when wstrb[1]=0 and kept when wstrb[1]=1, so the lane strobe is inverted.
awready resets to 1, so awready is 1 during reset and in the cycle ending at R1, and an AW transfer could occur at R1.
Inverted reset condition on the register block: registers are not cleared on reset and are held at 0 in normal operation, so writes never take effect.
bvalid is set to 1 instead of cleared at the B transfer, so bvalid stays high after Eb and a second B transfer occurs.
Registers are written on every edge except Ec, so a register changes without a write and does not change at Ec.
arready resets to 1, so arready is 1 during reset and in the cycle ending at R1, and an AR transfer could occur at R1.
rdata and rresp are captured on every edge except the AR transfer, so the response is not the value sampled at Ear and changes under back-pressure.
Byte lane 2 is written when wstrb[2]=0 and kept when wstrb[2]=1, so the lane strobe is inverted.
bvalid is cleared on every edge without a B transfer and not at the B transfer, so bvalid drops under back-pressure or stays high after Eb.
Held write data and strobes are captured when there is no W transfer, not when there is, so a write whose AW arrives later uses wrong data or strobes.
